user_reviews.title: Kia Seltos
user_reviews.author: Dibyendu Chakraborty
user_reviews.text: Best SUV Owning the Kia New Seltos HTX A Petrol DCT (2026) with ADAS has been a thoroughly satisfying experience so far, blending style, comfort, and advanced technology in a well-rounded package. From the moment I took delivery, the car stood out with its bold and modern design. The sharp LED lighting, signature grille, and overall road presence make it look premium and eye-catching. The 1.5L turbo petrol engine paired with the DCT gearbox delivers a smooth yet responsive driving experience. In city traffic, the automatic transmission feels convenient and reduces fatigue, while on highways, the car accelerates confidently with minimal lag. The steering is light at low speeds and becomes stable as the speed increases, making it suitable for both urban and long-distance driving. One of the highlights of this variant is the ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems). Features like lane keep assist, forward collision warning, and adaptive cruise control add a layer of safety and confidence, especially during highway drives. While these features are still relatively new in this segment, they work effectively and enhance the overall driving experience. Inside the cabin, the Seltos offers a premium feel with high-quality materials and a well-designed dashboard. The infotainment system is intuitive, responsive, and packed with features, including smartphone connectivity. The ventilated seats, spacious cabin, and refined ride quality make long journeys comfortable for both driver and passengers. In terms of practicality, the boot space is adequate, and the car offers good ground clearance for Indian roads. Fuel efficiency is decent for a turbo petrol automatic, though it depends on driving style and traffic conditions. Overall, the Kia Seltos HTX A Petrol DCT with ADAS is a feature-loaded, stylish, and comfortable SUV that offers excellent value for money. It is ideal for those looking for a modern vehicle with advanced safety features and a smooth automatic driving experience.

user_reviews.title: Powerful Turbo Petrol DCT with Premium Comfort
user_reviews.author: Sachin Mohan
user_reviews.text: The Kia Seltos HTK(O) Turbo Petrol DCT impressed me with its sporty performance, smooth 7-speed DCT gearbox, and premium road presence. The turbo-petrol engine feels powerful during overtakes and highway cruising, while the automatic transmission makes city driving stress-free. The cabin is spacious, comfortable, and packed with useful features for daily use. Ride quality is well balanced, and the steering feels confident at higher speeds. Safety features and build quality inspire confidence on long trips. Mileage is decent for a turbo petrol automatic when driven sensibly. Overall, the Seltos HTK(O) DCT offers a great blend of performance, comfort, practicality, and value, making it an excellent family SUV for both city and highway driving.

user_reviews.title: Absolutely worth it
user_reviews.author: Ak
user_reviews.text: I recently bought a new Kia Seltos and I’m happy with it so far. It looks modern, drives comfortably in the city and on the highway, and the tech is easy to use. Fuel economy has been solid and the interior is practical for daily use. It’s not the most powerful or premium feeling, but for the price it offers good value. I’m satisfied with my purchase.

user_reviews.title: Seltos Review (odo 2200kms)
user_reviews.author: Suriya
user_reviews.text: This is my first car which is definitely a VFM.After driving for over 2000 km, the car handles highway and potholes well even for city driving it's handling is good . Talking about interiors it feels premium even for a base model and the physical buttons for AC controls is what I appreciate the most which doesn't take you away from your driving and for this price you are also getting cruise control which is a cherry on the top. The few nehs are not adjustable headrest and rear seat armrest for rear seats.Other than this I am loving this beast of a machine kudos to kia to make this affordable.

user_reviews.title: Luxury on a Budget: My Honest Take on the Kia Seltos Petrol Base
user_reviews.author: Shivam Singh
user_reviews.text: Buying the Kia Seltos Petrol HTE was seamless. It looks premium, drives smoothly in cities, and offers great safety. While it lacks features, its road presence and low maintenance are unbeatable.  On the road, the 1.5L engine is remarkably refined, offering a silent and vibration-free experience at idle. While it isn't a high-speed powerhouse, it handles daily commutes with ease and maintains great stability on highways. The steering feels light and responsive, making it easy to manoeuvre through tight spots. Inside, the cabin quality is impressive for a base trim. Even without the fancy touchscreens of higher models, the fit and finish remain top-tier. You get a sense of "big car" comfort with ample legroom and a high seating position that gives you a clear view of the road ahead, ensuring confidence for new drivers. Maintenance has been surprisingly light on the pocket. With Kia's transparent service costs and a widespread network, keeping the car in top shape is hassle-free. As long as you follow a regular service schedule and keep an eye on tyre pressure, the Seltos remains a reliable and stylish companion for years.

user_reviews.title: Booked New Seltos 2026 HTK Optional IVT
user_reviews.author: Aniket Jadhav
user_reviews.text: Kia Seltos Facelift has emerged as the best default choice for a mid-size SUV suitable as a family car and for enthusiasts too. It has a proven track record, best fit and finish in the segment, a reliable machine, improved suspension and elevated comfort. It is loaded with features, necessary tech and rugged looks right from the lower variants. Design is not as polarising as Syros, in fact, it is more futuristic and has a much bolder stance. It borrows design and aesthetics from its globally popular EV siblings, which makes it more desirable at this price range. Competition in this class is prone to reliability issues, after-sales service and less desirable to sophisticated metro customers. It's definitely going to rule the roads till the next Creta facelift shows up!

user_reviews.title: Sophistication Meets Efficiency – My 2026 Seltos Diesel AT Experience
user_reviews.author: Deepak P
user_reviews.text:
After driving the 2026 Kia Seltos Diesel Automatic for a few weeks, I can confidently say Kia has nailed the formula for a premium mid-size SUV.
​What I Loved:
​The Transmission: Unlike some jerky AMTs or loud CVTs, this 6-speed Automatic (Torque Converter) is silent and very predictable.
​Tech Overload: The dual 12.3-inch screens are crisp and lag-free. Having a dedicated 5-inch screen just for climate control is a genius ergonomic touch.
​Presence: The new "Digital Tiger Face" and the "Star Map" LED tail lights give it a futuristic, aggressive look that turns heads.
​Comfort: The ride quality is much more balanced now—firm enough for high-speed stability but soft enough to soak up road patches comfortably.
​Points to Note:
The Diesel engine is built for efficiency rather than outright "sporty" speed. While it’s not a race car, it’s a very competent cruiser. Also, the gloss black interior bits look amazing but do catch fingerprints easily!
​Final Thoughts:
If you want a car that looks like it's from 2030 but has the reliability and range of a classic diesel, the 2026 Seltos is the way to go.

user_reviews.title: performance apt for city drive
user_reviews.author: Archit Gupta
user_reviews.text: Driving the Kia Seltos GTX Automatic CVT has been a surprisingly refined and comfortable experience. The first thing that stands out is how smooth the CVT gearbox feels in daily city driving. Traffic conditions, especially in crowded urban roads, become much less tiring because the transmission delivers power seamlessly without jerks. The steering feels light at low speeds, making parking and tight turns easy, while still offering decent confidence on highways. The cabin quality is another major highlight of the Seltos GTX variant. The interiors feel premium with well-designed seats, a modern dashboard layout, and a feature-loaded infotainment system. Ventilated seats, panoramic sunroof, Bose sound system, and the digital instrument cluster together create a very upscale driving environment. Kia has clearly focused on making the experience luxurious without pushing the car into an unaffordable segment. Performance-wise, the engine is more tuned for smoothness and comfort rather than aggressive, sporty driving. The CVT responds well during normal acceleration, though enthusiastic drivers may sometimes miss the punch of a DCT gearbox during sudden overtakes. However, for regular commuting and long drives, the refinement level is excellent. The suspension absorbs bumps comfortably, and highway stability remains impressive even at higher speeds. Fuel efficiency is also quite reasonable for a feature-rich SUV of this size. Overall, the Kia Seltos GTX CVT feels like a perfect balance between premium comfort, practicality, modern technology, and ease of driving. It is an ideal choice for someone looking for a stylish and stress-free automatic SUV for both city and highway usage.
